Three phone calls just reshaped the entire US AI regulatory landscape.

Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk, and David Sacks called the president directly — hours before he was set to sign a new AI safety executive order. The order was scrapped. A White House source told Axios the president 'just hates regulation.'

So now there will be no comprehensive federal AI safety framework in 2026. Some will celebrate this as a green light for innovation. The reality is more complicated.

No federal standard does not mean no rules. It means fragmented rules. States are already drafting their own. The EU has its AI Act. Industry-specific regulators will step in where they see risk. For enterprises deploying AI across jurisdictions, this patchwork is arguably harder to manage than a single clear framework.

And in a striking contrast, the Vatican is publishing its first-ever encyclical on artificial intelligence this same week. Governance pressure is not going away — it is migrating from political to institutional channels.

The practical takeaway for executives: build your internal AI governance framework now, on your terms, before external rules force reactive scrambling.
